rfi.title: Israel accused of preventing births in Gaza as Amnesty seeks genocide probe
rfi.description: Israeli measures have prevented births in Gaza, Amnesty International said on Wednesday – calling for the International Criminal Court to investigate whether they amount to an act of genocide. In a report documenting the war’s devastating toll on women and girls, the rights group detailed the collapse of fertility services and deadly shortages of medicines needed during childbirth.

rfi.title: Women in France face steep financial hurdles to escaping domestic abuse: report
rfi.description: Money can be one of the biggest barriers to escaping domestic violence for women around the world. In France, leaving an abusive partner can cost a woman up to 11 months' salary in the first three months alone, a report published on Wednesday has found. Its authors are calling for greater public support, warning that the expense can prevent women from leaving or force some to return to violent partners.

rfi.title: France urged to put women's safety at heart of migration policies
rfi.description: France's High Council for Equality between Women and Men (HCE) is calling for gender to be a "central aspect" of migration policies, warning that the violence migrant women suffer throughout their journeys into exile is being ignored. The call comes as the world marks the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women on Wednesday.

rfi.title: PSG coach Luis Enrique urges squad to show resilience as Roma clash looms
rfi.description: Paris Saint-Germain head coach Luis Enrique called on his squad to embrace the challenge of fighting for trophies without key players such as Désiré Doué and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia as his team prepared for Wednesday night's visit of Roma in the Champions League.

rfi.title: Police officer to stand trial for murder over shooting of French teenager Nahel
rfi.description: A French police officer who shot and killed 17-year-old Nahel Merzouk during a traffic stop in June 2023 will stand trial for murder following a ruling by an appeals court. Tuesday’s ruling is the latest in a series of competing judicial rulings over a case that has for many become a symbol of police brutality in France.

rfi.title: Gisèle Pelicot to file legal complaint against publisher over nude photo use
rfi.description: Gisèle Pelicot said on Monday she was "deeply shocked" that nude photographs of her had been used without her consent to promote a psychoanalyst's essay on the concept of coercive control.

rfi.title: France to establish 'strategic stockpiles' of critical minerals
rfi.description: France will build up "strategic stocks" of rare earths and certain priority metals, inspired by the reserves that exist for oil, the presidency announced on Monday.

rfi.title: Senegal reclaim Africa Cup of Nations title after 11-month legal fight
rfi.description: Judges at the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) on Tuesday declared Senegal winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations.

rfi.title: Zambia formally indicts opposition leader on treason charges
rfi.description: Zambian prosecutors have formally indicted the country's main opposition leader and 12 others on treason charges over an alleged plot to overthrow the government. This comes three months after a contested election which saw incumbent President Hakainde Hichilema secure a second term.

rfi.title: From the track to the gallery: Dakar's autumn in the spotlight
rfi.description: This November, Dakar hosted two exceptional events: the Youth Olympic Games, which ran until 13 November, and Dak'Art, the Dakar Biennale of contemporary African art, which runs from 19 November to 19 December. The Games were the first Olympic event ever held on the African continent, and the Biennale now brings together artists from across Africa and its diaspora. In this episode, we hear from participants in both events.

rfi.title: Macron pledges €350m for aviation research in a bid for industrial acceleration
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron has announced €350 million in funding for civil aviation research and plans to create new industrial zones with simplified administrative procedures, as France looks to accelerate its re-industrialisation. The announcement came during the second Choose France business summit focused on the home market.

rfi.title: Zelensky calls for EU inclusion in talks with Russia 'as soon as possible'
rfi.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday called for new negotiations with Russia involving European leaders to be held as soon as possible and repeated a plea for his country to join the NATO alliance.

rfi.title: UN condemns drone strikes in Khartoum suspected to have come from Ethiopia
rfi.description: A United Nations building was one of several structures damaged in drone attacks on Sudan’s capital, Khartoum, which are suspected to have been launched from Ethiopia.

rfi.title: Major cyberattack hits IT systems at Guadeloupe university hospital
rfi.description: A major cyberattack has disrupted the university hospital in the French overseas department of Guadeloupe, affecting its operations and forcing it to activate its emergency response plan and postpone non-emergency procedures.

rfi.title: French pair target Grand Slam glory after ATP Finals crown in Turin
rfi.description: French tennis players Théo Arribagé and Albano Olivetti were on Monday setting their sights on playing in their country's Davis Cup team and trophies at the four Grand Slam tournaments next year, after capturing the doubles title at the 2026 men's end of season championships.

rfi.title: UN warns Libya must not become stage for Russia-Ukraine war after drone strikes
rfi.description: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday said his country was behind strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya, adding that one of them sank in the latest spillover from Moscow's war with Kyiv. The United Nations condemned Sunday's strikes and has called for an international investigation.

rfi.title: Cop31 climate talks collapse as EU rejects deal that omits fossil fuels
rfi.description: The Cop31 climate summit in Turkey has ended in disarray after the European Union and several other countries rejected a proposed global agreement that failed to explicitly mention fossil fuels. The breakdown, after more than two weeks of negotiations and a record 44 hours of overtime, marks a major setback for international climate diplomacy, with deep divisions over energy policy and financial support for developing nations left unresolved.

lemonde.description: Le 108ᵉ congrès des maires de France a pris une dimension très politique à l’approche de la présidentielle, alors que la majorité des candidats, à l’exception de Marine Le Pen et de Jean-Luc Mélenchon, a prévu de s’y rendre. lemonde.title: Budget 2027 : au Sénat, un vote inattendu sur la mise à contribution des retraités
lemonde.description: Contre l’avis du gouvernement et de la commission des finances, une partie de la droite et du centre droit a mêlé ses voix à celles de la gauche et de l’extrême droite pour s’opposer à la suppression totale de l’abattement fiscal dont bénéficient les retraités. lemonde.description: Le gratte-ciel symbole de Vision 2030 a été touché pour la deuxième fois en cinq jours, mardi 24 novembre. Cette attaque intervient alors qu’au Yémen voisin, les forces gouvernementales, soutenues par Riyad, reculent face aux houthistes, appuyés par les Iraniens.

lemonde.title: Entre Giorgia Meloni l’Italienne et Mette Frederiksen la Danoise, une convergence de position contre l’immigration
lemonde.description: Bien qu’issues de deux mouvances opposées – le néofascisme pour la présidente du conseil italien et la social-démocratie pour la première ministre danoise –, les deux dirigeantes, qui se retrouveront au conseil européen extraordinaire, jeudi 26 et vendredi 27 novembre, s’accordent sur un objectif : expulser davantage de migrants d’Europe.

lemonde.title: En Espagne, pays aux avant-postes du changement climatique, l’environnement reste le grand absent de la campagne électorale
lemonde.description: Malgré les catastrophes climatiques à répétition, la lutte contre le réchauffement peine à s’imposer dans le débat public, victime des clivages politiques qui fracturent le pays, et alors que des élections législatives anticipées doivent se tenir dimanche 29 novembre.

lemonde.title: L’Union européenne veut se doter d’une stratégie industrielle sur l’informatique quantique
lemonde.description: La Commission a présenté, mercredi 25 novembre, le Quantum Act, un plan qui vise à accélérer le passage à l’usage industriel de cette technologie capable de traiter des quantités de données plus importantes que l’informatique actuelle.

lemonde.title: Prix Penser le travail 2026 : les nouveaux visages de la subordination des salariés
lemonde.description: Le prix Penser le travail, cofondé par Sciences Po et « Le Monde », doit être décerné mercredi 25 novembre. Dans leurs ouvrages respectifs, les trois finalistes, Marion Flécher, Maud Simonet et Clément Pouré, interrogent différentes tendances du management moderne.

lemonde.title: Plans d’épargne-retraite : une économie d’impôt à soupeser
lemonde.description: A priori très avantageuse, la mécanique fiscale qui permet de déduire ses cotisations de son revenu imposable est à plusieurs ressorts. Son mode d’emploi mérite une lecture attentive pour un usage optimal.

lemonde.title: L’influenceur Tibo InShape dépose plainte à la suite d’une action devant son domicile revendiquée par un groupuscule identitaire
lemonde.description: L’action a été revendiquée par Le « mouvement de la jeunesse identitaire toulousaine » Furie. Le youtubeur fait l’objet d’attaques en ligne depuis la publication d’une vidéo avec une coach sportive portant le drapeau français en guise de voile.

france24fr.title: Violences faites aux femmes : 129 femmes tuées par un proche chaque jour dans le monde en 2025
france24fr.description: Selon un rapport de l'ONU publié mardi, quelque 47 000 femmes et filles ont été tuées par des proches en 2025, soit environ cinq par heure ou 129 par jour. Alors que les femmes ont représenté 19 % des victimes d'homicides dans le monde, 60 % d'entre elles ont été tuées dans la sphère privée.

france24fr.title: "Aux combattantes inconnues assassinées par le patriarcat" : un hommage aux victimes des féminicides

france24fr.title: Plus de 840 millions de femmes et de filles ont subi des violences dans le monde
france24fr.description: Chaque 25 novembre, la Journée internationale pour l'élimination des violences faites aux femmes rappelle la nécessité de lutter contre toutes ses formes, encore trop présentes : dans le monde, 840 millions de femmes et de filles ont subi des violences physiques ou sexuelles. france24fr.title: Paris Nautic Show : quelle industrie nautique en France ?

phys-org.title: Ant rivalry temporarily protects native ants until one invader takes over
phys-org.description: When an invasive species enters a natural habitat, it can start competing for resources with native species and threaten their survival. If more than one invasive species occupies the same habitat, the interactions between them can further contribute to the damage and disruption that ensues.

phys-org.title: California braces for flooding threat from huge tides, El Niño
phys-org.description: Californians are preparing for a confluence of exceptionally high tides and El Niño-fueled weather that threatens coastal areas with extreme flooding during the busiest U.S. travel week of the year.

phys-org.title: Japan unveils rover prototype for moon water mission
phys-org.description: Japan's space agency unveiled Wednesday a test model of a rover that will travel to the moon's south pole in a search for water, which could potentially be used for rocket fuel.

phys-org.title: China launches Shenzhou 24 spacecraft carrying 2 Chinese and 1 Pakistani astronaut
phys-org.description: China on Wednesday launched the Shenzhou 24 spacecraft with three astronauts—two Chinese and a Pakistani—sending the first foreign crew member to its space station.

phys-org.description: What makes people support a carbon price? To find out, 108 researchers, led by a research team at the University of Innsbruck, Austria, tested 55 different ideas at the same time, from information campaigns to reflection tasks. On average, there was a small but statistically significant positive effect. Individually, the effect was detectable for only 11 of the 55 ideas. phys-org.title: New EU Bureaucracy Index: EU law has more than doubled since 2010
phys-org.description: The new EU Bureaucracy Index measures the volume of EU law in force, and it shows a record high: At the end of 2025, the EU regulations and directives in force comprised around 47,600 standard pages, 118% more than in 2010. The volume of EU law has thus more than doubled in 15 years, and it continued to grow in 2025. The main drivers are sanctions regulations and new sets of rules in environmental, consumer and health law.

phys-org.title: Queensland keeps learning disaster lessons. So why do we keep forgetting them?
phys-org.description: After an early start to Queensland's storm season, with severe storms and flooding already affecting communities across the state, attention is once again turning to disaster preparedness and response.

phys-org.title: A star's 'obliquity' likely has little impact on a given planet's habitability
phys-org.description: A star's axial tilt as it relates to the circumstellar disk that surrounds it is known as stellar obliquity. Over space and time, there are a myriad of solar-type stars with all sorts of obliquities. But the question heretofore has always been what effect a given star's initial obliquity has on the planetary system that forms around it.

phys-org.title: What draws data centers to a community?
phys-org.description: As Oklahoma communities weigh new data center development, research co-authored by a University of Oklahoma architecture professor offers insight into what draws major technology companies to locations—and why those choices matter locally.

phys-org.title: Hurricane season wrap-up: El Niño fueled record number of Pacific storms but calmed Atlantic
phys-org.description: The 2026 hurricane season, which officially ends on Nov. 30, will be remembered as a year of contrasts between the Atlantic and Pacific, a classic indication of a hurricane season influenced by a very strong El Niño. Below-normal activity across the Atlantic basin was offset by above-average activity in the Pacific, including two disasters in Hawaii.

phys-org.title: Ultrathin 'rainbow' sails could power spacecraft and shade the Earth
phys-org.description: For years, whimsically minded space enthusiasts have been dreaming of sailing across the vastness of the void on beams of sunlight. Photons, the massless particles that make up those beams of sunlight, still carry momentum and can therefore impart a gentle push when they bounce off a surface. This force is the concept behind "solar sailing," which has been having a bit of a moment in the last decade as several proof-of-concept flights have shown it is indeed feasible.

phys-org.title: How alfalfa forms root nodules without rhizobia
phys-org.description: A research team led by professor Feng Jian at the Institute of Genetics and Developmental Biology (IGDB) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences has uncovered a cytokinin–NODULE INCEPTION (NIN) regulatory module associated with spontaneous root nodule formation in alfalfa (Medicago sativa).

phys-org.title: Laser light reveals where electrons accumulate in atomically thin semiconductor stacks
phys-org.description: Stacking semiconductors—the chips that power phones, computers and so much more—enables quicker signal movement with less energy, but how does the process actually work? Turns out shining a literal light on the semiconducting materials can help elucidate how the electrons move in the stack, according to a multi-institutional team in Japan. The approach could help inform the development of more efficient, low-power electronics, the researchers said.

phys-org.description: Earthquakes are full of unknowns—scientists can't accurately predict exactly when or where the next big earthquake will strike. undark.title: Aftershock: Untangling the Risks of Electroconvulsive Therapy
undark.description: Psychiatrists and other experts, backed by studies, maintain that ECT is safe and effective for severe psychiatric conditions including depression, schizophrenia, and bipolar disorder. But some ECT patients report lasting cognitive harm and say they weren’t adequately warned of potential side effects.

undark.title: Australia’s Social Media Ban Has Not Worked — For Now
undark.description: New data coming out of Australia suggests that bans alone may not be an effective enough deterrent to stop children from using social media. But the research faces limitations. What does that mean for other countries considering similar restrictions?

undark.title: Body Snatchers and the Murky Process of Whole-Body Donation
undark.description: Opinion | Each year, more than 20,000 people in the U.S. donate their bodies to science after death. But the programs that handle whole-body donations lack oversight, with inconsistencies in standards of consent, transparency, and accountability. The result is reminiscent of the body-snatching practices of years past.

undark.title: Book Review: The Bizarre Frontiers of Product Testing

undark.title: After Cancer, a Complex Aftermath for Survivors
undark.description: Around 70 percent of people with cancer today will live for more than five years after their diagnosis. They’re likely to find that life after cancer is complicated — marked by health risks and chronic illnesses — and that their primary care doctors may be ill-equipped to help them navigate it.

undark.title: Could an Amazonian Highway Open a Pandora’s Box of Pathogens?

But some scientists are concerned the project — which would likely increase access between humans, livestock, and wildlife — might be a biosecurity risk.

undark.title: Interview: The Nerve That Could Transform Medicine
undark.description: Kevin Tracey, a researcher and neurosurgeon whose team discovered the vagus nerve’s link to the immune system more than two decades ago, has developed an electrical implant to stimulate the nerve in an effort to help rheumatoid arthritis sufferers who currently have difficulty taking medications.

undark.title: AI and Virtual Reality Enter the Therapist’s Office
undark.description: Some experts say that deepfake technology and other AI tools could help tackle treatment-resistant conditions like anorexia and prolonged grief. But plenty of questions remain, including whether there could be damaging side effects and whether the therapy is even effective.

undark.title: On the Weather Radar: Cloudy With a Chance of Birds

undark.title: In a Long-Awaited Move, FDA Enforces Trial Result Transparency

proj-syn.title: Nvidia’s Liability Problem Isn’t Going Away
proj-syn.description: Given previous suspicions about Nvidia's engagement with China, one wonders if Jensen Huang’s admitted extramarital affairs are just a cover-up for more consequential violations and misrepresentations. Whatever the case, the problem is not limited to Huang; with his reinstatement as CEO, it involves the company's entire board.

proj-syn.title: Mapping Strategic Supply-Chain Risk
proj-syn.description: If there is a premium to be paid for resilient supply chains, who will foot the bill? The answer can be found through a three-stage approach of identifying current vulnerabilities, letting markets and public tenders price them, and then having national-security authorities intervene only where market pricing fails.

proj-syn.title: Holiday 2026 Reading List
proj-syn.description: In the bi-weekly PS Book Recommendations newsletter—available for free to all registered PS readers—we highlight insightful, informative, or otherwise compelling books, written or recommended by PS contributors. Here, we present a selection of recent works by PS contributors that are worth adding to your holiday shopping list (and your bookshelf).

proj-syn.title: The Summit of Self-Promotion
proj-syn.description: Despite claiming that world history was made in Shenzhen with the US–Russia–China Heads of State Declaration toward Peace, the trilateral summit between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump, and Vladimir Putin was about optics, not substance. One of the many important problems they failed to address was China’s export-led growth.

proj-syn.title: Why Nvidia Couldn’t Quit Jensen Huang
proj-syn.description: Developing AI requires tremendous coordination across firms and sectors, from the AI labs themselves to energy and computing infrastructure, as well as long-term vision and patience. Whereas much of this coordination and planning is led by the government in China, in the US, it has been driven largely by one CEO.

proj-syn.title: Chips Too Big to Fail
proj-syn.description: The Trump administration pushed for Jensen Huang to be reinstated as CEO of Nvidia to keep the stock market high, to feed a possible productivity surge, and to advance a US foreign policy built on reconciliation with China. But will Americans continue to believe in the AI miracle and this new version of Chimerica?

proj-syn.title: Amplifying the Voice of Human Limits
proj-syn.description: Tech leaders like Elon Musk have embraced Prometheus as a symbol of creation, conquest, and discovery. But the Promethean impulse must be balanced by the “Orphic” tradition’s respect for and contemplation of nature’s mystery.

proj-syn.title: Making the Most of South Korea’s Semiconductor Boom
proj-syn.description: The AI boom has driven South Korea’s economic growth well above expectations, thanks to soaring demand for advanced semiconductors. But AI’s transformative potential does not guarantee that the current investment frenzy will continue, leaving the economy vulnerable to a downturn.

proj-syn.title: Is a Financial-Market Reckoning Imminent?
proj-syn.description: After a year of unprecedented AI investment, increasingly financed by debt in opaque private markets, growing unease about the industry’s future is reflected in sharp declines in the NASDAQ index and the S&P 500. But the stock market’s dependence on a handful of highly leveraged companies—and even a single CEO—is hardly the only source of global financial risk. Amid mounting fears, we asked PS contributors what to expect from financial markets in the year ahead.

proj-syn.title: The African Union’s Elusive Quest for Security
proj-syn.description: The African Union has long sought to implement Ali Mazrui’s concept of Pax Africana, but has faced persistent logistical and financial constraints. The key to making peacekeeping operations more effective is establishing a better division of labor between the AU, the United Nations, and regional African organizations.

proj-syn.title: The Achilles’ Heel of Emerging Economies’ Trade
proj-syn.description: New research shows that 23% of global goods imports in 2024 faced at least two of three vulnerabilities: product criticality, supply concentration, and geopolitical distance. Given the wide range of problems, early diagnosis and targeted action are particularly important for emerging economies with limited fiscal space.

proj-syn.title: AI Agents Could Make Big Tech Bigger
proj-syn.description: The rise of agentic AI could give a handful of Big Tech firms unprecedented power over our personal lives. Unless lawmakers and regulators act now, these digital gatekeepers could manipulate consumers, turbocharge corporate surveillance, and threaten our individual rights and civil liberties.

proj-syn.title: If the AI Bubble Is Bursting, the Fallout Will Be Severe
proj-syn.description: With the S&P 500 following the tech-heavy NASDAQ into correction territory, even as Anthropic set a record with its initial public offering, this is a good moment to compare AI stock valuations with earlier asset-price bubbles. A look back at the dot-com boom and bust of the late 1990s offers ample cause for concern.

proj-syn.title: Journalism Can Be More Than AI Fodder
proj-syn.description: As AI fundamentally alters the information environment, news publishers risk becoming little more than content suppliers for Big Tech. To avoid that fate, many are drawing on their archives and expertise to develop AI tools that allow them to operate and compete on their own terms.

proj-syn.title: Governing African Economies as They Are
proj-syn.description: Africa cannot overcome its development challenges by applying the same knowledge, economic, and innovation systems that helped create them. Imagining and governing new ways forward will require three intellectual ruptures.

proj-syn.title: Making Earth Cool Again
proj-syn.description: Climate multilateralism is evolving into a two-tiered system in which high-level negotiations toward shared commitments and the real-world implementation of climate solutions become more mutually supportive. Only by unleashing such virtuous cycles can we keep the 1.5ºC target for global warming within reach.

proj-syn.title: America’s Lame-Duck Autocrat
proj-syn.description: When autocrats suffer a defeat, they tend to double down, such as by intensifying repression at home or behaving more recklessly abroad. With two years left in office after historic midterm election losses, this is the road US President Donald Trump appears to be taking.

proj-syn.title: Getting Ukraine’s House in Order
proj-syn.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has repeatedly opposed the idea of forming a national unity government. But bringing opposition leaders into the cabinet would ensure the checks on corruption and wayward bureaucratic action that Zelensky’s team can no longer provide.
